acceptance: An attempt whose only `401` text comes from pull request content is not classified as auth; a test feeds a real-shaped omp failure whose output contains a diff line with `401` and expects the error kind.
A genuine gateway or provider 401 is still classified as auth (existing calibrated fixtures keep passing).
context: Found while running the first gateway canary after #3296 merged. Root cause of the underlying failure was the tailnet ACL (tag:oracle-ci allowed only tcp:8765, not tcp:4000); the misclassification is independent of that.
description: The OMP auth absence pattern `401[^\n]{0,80}` (absence.CALIBRATED_AUTH_PATTERNS) matches any `401` in the text it scans, including pull request content echoed into the reviewer's output. On 2026-10-23 the attempt for PR #3332 (head ece15c335, run 39952339xxx family; oracle-verdict status `large: absent (auth: 401 | `ORACLE_GATEWAY_TOKEN` does not match `client.token`. Run `secrets`. |\n+| Ga)`) failed with omp exit code 1 because the tailnet policy did not open the gateway port. The same failure on PR #3331 in run 39951571685 was recorded correctly as `error: exit code 1`. The `+|` prefix in the captured detail shows it is a diff line from the PR's new troubleshooting table, not an HTTP response. An auth absence is treated differently from an error (auth absences are excluded from the same-reviewer retry), so diff text can change retry behavior and mislead diagnosis.
